items.q: I had Phil Wilson, the trombone player who played with Woody Herman

ctx.x: What did you gain from Berklee?

Berklee was great. I mean I’ll be honest, and this is not a criticism of Berklee, the best I got was the jam sessions at night and stuff, after school and stuff. I played with all — I mean I played really out to lunch, avante garde stuff, which I still like a lot of that because it’s — like for me “Heart and Soul,” if it’s in there it’s great. The form doesn’t matter to me so much. I love like what we’re doing up here with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. But and in the classes I was just starting to write music,…

how I was going to do it, you know, so I just like I fell into that Stevie Wonder gig. And the funny thing is I went from one to another and the cost of living was nothing like it is now. God, like I don’t know how people do it now. I mean you’ve certainly got to make a lot of money going out of school. So I went to New York, and the hardest times were when some lean times hit, like in the early 90s or something, where I never did the thing where I’d do other gigs to figure out how to do it.
